en.title: Minimum Splits to Make an Array Non-Decreasing
en.description:
One operation splits a positive integer into two positive integers whose sum equals the original number, inserted in place in the chosen order; pieces can be split further. Find the minimum number of operations needed to make the whole array non-decreasing.

The input/output and examples are compiled by CSWork; numeric ranges marked as this site's are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: This site's standard input: the first line contains n (1..100000); the second line contains n positive integers (1..10⁹).
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: split 10 into 5, 5 to get 5, 5, 5, 8, in one operation. Example 2: splitting 9 into 3, 3, 3 takes two operations and gives a non-decreasing array of all 3s. Example 3: the array is already sorted, so no split is needed.
hints: Process from right to left. With limit as the upper bound allowed by the right side, the current value v needs at least ceil(v/limit) parts; split it as evenly as possible, and the new leftmost value is floor(v/parts), which becomes the upper bound for the next step.
